Pursuant to State and County Directives, San Gabriel City Hall is closed to the public and physical access
to the meeting has been suspended. To provide members of the public access to the meeting and an
opportunity to comment on items on and off the Agenda, the following opportunities have been
established:

Public Comments

Please email all public comments to Lhakobian@sgch.org and include the following on the subject line of
your email: the section (Public Comment, Consent, Public Hearing, Continued Business, New Business) and
Item Number you are commenting on. The Staff will read public comments into the record for up to the
three-minute limit. Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read.
Example: PUBLIC COMMENT: New Business Item A
Watch the Meeting Online
Live broadcasts of the meetings are available using the following link:

https://www.youtube.com/CityofSanGabriel

   COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION
  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, MAY 3, 2021

   CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Cabot called the regular meeting of the Community Services
  Commission to order at 6:31 p.m. on Monday, May 3, 2021 with all
  Commissioners and staff participating by teleconference.

   PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Chair Cabot.

   ROLL CALL

  Absent: Commissioner Fang
  Present: Chair Cabot, Vice Chair Velazquez, Commissioners Cheung von
  Haam and Huerta.

1.  PRESENTATION

  A. Recognition of Outgoing Commissioners

  Presented by Community Services Manager, Lucy Hakobian

    Commissioner Cheung von Haam thanked everyone for their
  comradeship.
    Chair Cabot thanked Commissioner Cheung von Haam for her time
  on the Commission.

  B. COVID-19 Update

  Presented by Community Services Manager, Lucy Hakobian

  C. Reopening Protocols

  Presented by Community Services Manager, Lucy Hakobian

    Chair Cabot asked for clarification about pods at Community
  Services events. She also inquired about future concerts.

2.  PUBLIC COMMENT
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54954.3, this is the time approved for
  members of the public to address the Community Services Commission on items
  of interest that are within the subject matter jurisdiction of the Community Services
  Commission of the City of San Gabriel. The Commission cannot take action on
  such comment but may put an item on a future agenda.
   If you wish to address the Community Services Commission, e-mail all public
  comments to LHakobian@sgch.org.

  Public comment by George Young, San Gabriel Sea Gulls Head Coach. He
  provided an update on the Sea Gulls, they are having club age group
  swimming at surrounding high schools. These schools include Gabrielino,
  Mark Keppel, Temple City & Bishop Amat HS. SGSG also has a partnership
  with the YMCA of West San Gabriel Valley, together they will be training
  American Red Cross lifeguards for shallow water lifeguarding They are also
  working together to promote water safety in the San Gabriel Valley.

    Chair Cabot is impressed with everything the swim team has been
  able to accomplish during the pandemic.

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  MINUTES OF THE COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION MEETING OF
  APRIL 2021.

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the last Community
  Services Commission meeting.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  Motion made by Vice Chair Velazquez, seconded by Commissioner Huerta.
  Minutes of the Community Services Commission Meeting from April were
  approved.

4.  NEW BUSINESS

  A. SELFLESS VOLUNTEER AWARD
  Presented by Community Services Supervisor, Christina Alatorre
    Chair Cabot believes volunteers who reside outside of San Gabriel
  should be eligible for the award if they contribute to the SG
  community.
    Commissioner Huerta agrees that these volunteers should be
  eligible.

  Motion made by Vice Chair Velazquez, seconded by Commissioner Cheung
  von Haam to extend the eligibility requirements to non-residents who
  contribute to our community.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 4-0.

   City of San Gabriel
  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  June 7, 2021

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Christina Alatorre, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  Monthly Department Report

Aquatics
The Community Services Department will continue to offer swim lessons for summer 2021.
Five cycles and a Saturday cycle will be offered June 14 through August 20. Registration
for lessons began on Tuesday, June 1. Lap Swim and Water Aerobics will also be offered
on Monday and Wednesday nights. All aquatic programs will follow all protocols set by
the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health.

Contract Classes
The Summer GUIDE has been released online. Registration for summer classes began
Tuesday, June 1. The issue of the Summer GUIDE is filled with exciting summer programs
for all ages, both in-person and virtual! All classes will follow protocols set by the Los
Angeles County Department of Public Health. The summer edition of the Guide features
Summer in San Gabriel, Parks Make Life Better month, youth camps and programs,
aquatics, classes and more!

Facilities/Picnic Rentals
The Community Services Department is now taking rentals for the Grapevine Arbor,
outdoor space only. The first rental is scheduled to take place on June 12. Staff are
ensuring that customers follow all Los Angeles County Department of Public Health’s
Reopening Protocols and submitting the event for approval on their behalf. The maximum
number of people currently allowed in the outdoor space is 200 people with
modifications. Staff are diligently preparing the facility to ensure it is well prepared for the
upcoming events.
Picnic Shelter Rentals are also gearing up with the first rental to take place on Saturday,
June 5. Customers and their guests are expected to follow all social distancing and
protocols from the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health.

  5-A
 Older Adult Programs
Older Adults are encouraged to join staff for Drive-in Bingo on the first and third Thursday
of each month at 10:00 am in the Mission Playhouse Parking Lot. Participants are also
welcome to join the fun each Friday at the Adult Recreation Center for Active Adult Table
Tennis from 9:00 am-12:00 pm.
The drive-thru meal program is still taking place in the Mission Playhouse Parking Lot. The
YWCA of San Gabriel Valley is preparing 7 meals with fruit and milk for 175 older adults
for distribution on Tuesday mornings. The City purchases 5 meals for approximately 50
people for distribution on Wednesdays. We have seen a decline in participation which
could potentially be attributed to the easing of County restrictions and the waning in the
COVID-19 surge.

Special Events
Outstanding Older American: Sally Baldwin was named San Gabriel’s Outstanding Older
American for 2021. Sally was recognized during the LA County Virtual Awards Ceremony
Honoring Older Adults in the Los Angeles Region on May 27, 2021. Mrs. Baldwin will be
recognized in San Gabriel for all of her services within the community at a later date.

Youth Programs
The San Gabriel Sports Academy will be offered for incoming 6 th-8th grade students at
Jefferson Middle School. This program will run 12:30-2:30 pm on Mondays and
Wednesdays from June 14 through August 4. This is a free program and registration is
required.

Art in the Park is a new youth and family program that will be offered at Smith and Vincent
Lugo Parks, in conjunction with the Summer in San Gabriel series. This program will
provide a craft and educational experience for all participants. This program will be
offered 5:30-6:30 pm on Tuesdays and Thursdays from June 22 through August 12. This
program is free. Pre-registration is highly encouraged.

The Virtual After School program has received recognition from the California Park and
Recreation Society District 13 as a recipient of the Health, Wellness and Community Life
Award for excellence and innovation. The Community Services Department mission
statement is, “Creatively enriching the lives of every person in San Gabriel through
exceptional programs and services, inviting spaces and community connection.” Due to
the pandemic, the Virtual After School Program continued to meet the Departments
mission by offering a virtual livestreamed program for San Gabriel youth. The program
taught San Gabriel youth about different countries, traditions, and cultures through

  5-A
 videos, crafts, food and activities. The Virtual After School Program was selected by a
committee of park and recreation professionals.
